A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAE study. Their complete main texts, figures, equations, references, and appendices are readable and support matching content across substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic SAE experiments, LLM SAE training and sparse-probing results, and an analysis of publicly listed SAE sparsities.

after.justification: v4 retains original toy-model and LLM experiments and adds results investigating the interaction between SAE width and L0.

M1.justification: The documented automatic L0 optimizer changes its objective from input-dependent nth decoder projection in v3 Appendix A.11 to decoder-only pairwise cosine similarity in v4 Appendix I. The alternative nth-projection method is removed entirely. These change the auxiliary selection procedure's feedback and required inputs; the SAE architectures and primary c_dec formula remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic feature-recovery tasks, Pile activations, Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b settings, sparse-probing tasks, and SAE inventory. The new narrow-SAE experiment uses the existing 50-feature data with a different model width. Biology and chemistry are suggested applications, not new evaluations.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix A.9 evaluates nth decoder projection as an alternative to c_dec and discusses their relative behavior; this auxiliary diagnostic comparison is removed. Ground-truth SAE comparisons and the BatchTopK-versus-JumpReLU comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: v4 adds a 25-latent SAE protocol with K ranging from 1 to 20 on the existing 50-feature toy model. Figure 4 changes reconstruction evaluation from variance explained to MSE. The nth-projection evaluations across N and Gemma layer-20 k=1 probing are removed. Retained LLM training budgets and settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds an analysis testing how insufficient SAE width interacts with L0 and residual feature hedging. Conversely, v3's alternative-metric validation and extensive sensitivity analyses over projection rank N disappear. The L0-transition experiment is retained, moving from Appendix A.8 to Section 3.5.

E5.justification: The retained Gemma layer-20 k=16 plot loses its explicit Mean and ±1 standard-deviation legend between v3 Figure 21 and v4 Figure 19, although shading remains. Elsewhere, the reported five-seed toy experiments, three-seed LLM sweeps, and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v4 adds narrow-SAE feature-recovery and c_dec results around the predicted L0 of 7.6, while removing nth-projection results and layer-20 k=1 probing scores. Figure 4 reports MSE instead of variance explained. The central retained results remain stable, including the trained-versus-ground-truth MSE values of 2.73 versus 4.88 in Section 3.3.

T1.justification: The new Theorem F.2 extends the two-feature analysis to arbitrary feature counts, proving a local descent direction under tied, bias-free Top-K assumptions and an active-but-excluded co-occurrence condition. The existing two-feature and c_dec proofs remain; the Gaussian nth-projection theorem is removed. New Remark F.3's negative-direction claim for anti-correlation conflicts with the positive conditional product in Equation 52.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims about incorrect L0, feature mixing, misleading reconstruction tradeoffs, and diagnostic guidance. The Discussion adds a qualified implication that low-L0 feature mixing may explain unreliable SAE-based steering and model editing.

C2.justification: v4 adds an explanation linking steering failures to mixtures outside the training distribution and interprets optimal L0 as width-dependent. It explicitly discusses imperfect high-L0 agreement with probing, recommends combining c_dec with downstream evaluations, and identifies unlabeled applications. Appendix A newly discloses that Top-K SAEs were not separately evaluated.

D1.justification: Appendix B clarifies that the pre-encoder subtraction reuses the decoder bias already shown in the equations. The nth-projection pseudocode and N-specific tuning guidance are removed; c_dec pseudocode remains. Existing learning rates, warmup information, and experiment-repository access are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds substantial positioning against classical dictionary identifiability and recovery work, including Gribonval and Schnass, Donoho and Elad, Spielman et al., Wang et al., and Wu and Yu, plus elastic-net grouping. It replaces the philosophical critique of MDL-SAEs with a fixed-width selection/reconstruction objection and adds criticism of AFA's high L0.

P1.justification: v4 reorganizes the appendices into standalone lettered sections, moves limitations to their beginning, promotes the L0-transition experiment into the main narrative, and removes the alternative-metric branch. The Discussion is substantially rewritten, with additional introductory refinements and updated author and publication text.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with widespread figure resizing and relocation. The transition heatmaps become vertically stacked, Figure 4 changes its metric axis, narrow-SAE figures are added, and projection figures disappear. The layer-20 display contracts from four panels to two.

improvement.justification: The new width analysis and clearer limits and recommendations for c_dec modestly improve the support and practical guidance for L0 selection. The generalized descent argument also extends the earlier two-feature treatment. These gains are tempered by removal of the layer-20 k=1 validation and by Remark F.3's unsupported anti-correlation sign claim, which conflicts with Equation 52. The central LLM evidence remains largely unchanged.
